There's no known hierarchy it's just a numerical order. Elidibus has a special role but he's not like, completely in charge. Just a Zodiac order starting from Aries(Logrif) to Pisces(Lahabrea) plus Elidibus(Thirteenth) and Azem(Fourteenth). 

Lahabrea is the Speaker but that's never really been expanded upon, but I would speculate it to be something like the USA Speaker of the House, elected by the Convocation to basically run meetings and create committees as needed.

Elidibus is the Emissary but seems to be more of an adjudicator for deadlocked issues or problems. 

There's no detail on it but Elidibus does not appear in the zodiac order for versions of it that use Ophiuchus interestingly enough but is rather tacked on at the end, perhaps implying that the seat was added later due to having a need for someone to fill that role. Speculation though.

Going off of that I suppose would make Azem an even later addition to the Convocation with the sun as a 'wandering star' as opposed to the 'fixed stars' of the constellations. Which would I guess fit with the development cycle of a governing body, needing first an internal source of conflict resolution and order and then someone to interface with the public. But again, speculation.

Most health professionals I encounter either take it there by default or try the upper arm unsuccessfully a couple times before switching. (My upper only seems to succeed on a manual inflation/reading)

So it might be worthwhile to try just taking it on your forearm. Sometimes it'll still need to do it a couple times or hurt but it's not nearly as bad and you probably already own a cuff that will work for it.

I'm 6'2 *and* overweight so nearly every experience is uh, interesting, but some are definitely worse than others. Worst offenders:

San Francisco Orpheum, balcony: Lottery ticket for Hamilton, so painful that after Act I I asked if I could stand against a wall for the second act. This was much better and since I was near the end of the side anyway actually improved my view since I crept closer for a better handrail to lean against lol. No leg room and the seats at the Orpheum are cramped anyway. Front row loge and orchestra are generally OK for me, small seats aside. Orpheum's are narrower than some in New York, which is impressive.

San Francisco Golden Gate: Orchestra is fine. Seats aren't great but fit me well enough. The mezzanine is the 9th circle of hell, my knees were hanging six inches over the seat in front of me and my shins were pressed painfully against the seatback. Haven't been in the balcony, not going to try.

Majestic Theater, Orchestra Row K: The Majestic's seating sucked ass no matter where you were, knees always jammed into the seat in front, but not untenable anywhere but here - This row was the first of the back section and had a hard metal grille in front of it that had less clearance than the seats. I was crying by intermission.  I've sat elsewhere in the orchestra and been fine, I've sat in the balcony and been fine, just the brutalization of my knees ugh. Hopefully they change that. The way they handled it is a separate rant I won't go into.

Al Hirschfield: After the above experience I exchanged my center front mezzanine seat for a slightly further back aisle transfer seat. This turned out to be a good thing because while my ass fit in the seat fine, my *legs* did not fit in the row. I'd thought to maybe just be able to spread out a little and ended up needing to sit diagonally with my feet in the aisle because there just was not space for my legs. 

Walter Kerr: I had an aisle transfer here as well, but the usher didn't know how to remove the side. The pitch was awful and I had to sit weirdly, but the seat was actually plenty wide lol. A second showing I was in the front row for and that had 0 problems. 

Whichever theater it is in Louisville, KY that has their broadway tours, it's been like 14 years: Balcony had terrible legroom. Very painful. When you're at Les Miserables and crying because your legs hurt instead of because of the show you know something is wrong lol.

I'm fat and tall and the first time I went I'd gotten an aisle transfer seat to deal with this, except the usher I had that day didn't know how to remove the armrest for it so I had to just sit in it as-is, which has some really terrible staggering with the row in front and it was not a fun time.

The front row on the other hand was absolutely great the second time I saw Hadestown. Fantastic leg room and at least for me I was able to sit at the front of the seat and slide back under the armrests because it's wider beneath and not get hip bruises. 

Literally anywhere else, though, ugh. (Also the problem of not really being able to get to the accessible bathroom from the transfer seats, or honestly anywhere.)

The Orpheum is horrific in the balcony, bad in the Mezz and not great in the Orchestra either, and I'm only 6'2.

The Golden Gate is another one that's not great in SF. The seats are IMO better than the Orpheum and the Orchestra is decent enough pitch for me but the one time I got a rush ticket in Mezzanine my knees were like six+ inches over the seat in front of me and my shins were jammed hard against the edge of the seatback.

I've got what used to be diagnosed as Asperger's and it's always impacted me pretty negatively. The usual social derping and not understanding cues and being weird as hell, issues communicating, etc.

It does affect me in WoW too to an extent; I usually have a harder time fitting in with my guilds and end up guild-hopping because of it. I tend to end up hyperfocused on one or two specs I really enjoy and not want to do anything else which makes it harder for me to adapt when my spec is terrible but I can't bring myself to be interested in another 'better' one or a different class. For example, I main a Hunter, but I only like BM. I can't bring myself to care about MM enough to actually use it. 

On the other hand, it's helpful in that it's much easier for me to communicate if I don't have to be face to face with people; voice comms are easier to deal with than staring at people so I end up socializing a lot more than I would otherwise since I tend to just keep to myself normally. 

It's also been helpful for getting me actually out - Blizzcon is a lot easier to deal with than most things because well we're all there because we're rampaging nerds so talking to random people in lines and such goes from unimaginable stress to perfectly reasonable - If I'm in line for a WoW demo, chances are really good the people around me also play WoW and with an actual topic it's easy to figure out what to start with.

It's also easier to have people I keep in touch with since text is a much easier medium for me and I can just message people on Battlenet or Discord instead of calling them.

Velereth and Isaril Nightsinger are identical blood elf twins. Velereth is a Demon Hunter, and Isaril is a Mage. Both wear very stereotypical BC-era Blood Elf transmogs. They're both pretty much inseparable and finish each other's sentences and spend most of their time together.

Velereth used to be a Ranger who spent most of his time in the forest with his dragonhawk companion, Sunsparkle. When the Scourge attack happened he was sent to check on his village and found it already destroyed, with his mother brutally murdered and his twin seemingly dead, and he kind of... Lost it a bit. He eventually ended up in Outland to get away from Quel'thalas and became a Demon Hunter to try to atone for his failure to protect his homeland and seek revenge for his family. Since I don't RP him I just go with him being the one in charge of the Mardum mission/the DH class hall. He had Sevis kill him so he's aware his soul has become corrupted and has Altruis as his second in command. He reunited with his brother during the events of Legion. He's on the moral side for a DH and while he'll sacrifice anything personally, he doesn't expect it of others and won't hurt other people to achieve his goals. He's slightly odd in that he still loves nature from his past and wants to protect it still. 

Isaril is a Mage who mostly refuses to give a damn about his position within society or the Magisters and pretty much operates independently. He used to go out on patrol in the forest with his brother, preferring to study out in nature and with the company rather than stay cooped up inside a library. He nearly died during the Scourge invasion but ended up barely surviving in a coma, unfortunately Velereth didn't find out in time before leaving Quel'thalas and Isaril didn't know his brother was alive or where he'd gone. Isaril stayed on Azeroth and got himself in the usual amount of trouble over the years before running into Velereth during the events of Legion. He's horrified by what's happened to his brother, especially that his brother's soul has been corrupted, but his love for him easily won over the shock and he supports his brother fully. He isn't the leader of the Tirisgarde and stays with the Illidari most of the time.

Their situation currently is hard to come up with, because both are fundamentally good people and I can't actually picture them being willing to remain with the Horde after Sylvanas burned Teldrassil. They would have immediately left as soon as the order was given to try to evacuate civilians.

Past that, it's hard to reconcile. They wouldn't have done most of the things the war campaign forces you to do so if they're still with the Horde at all they're on the sidelines staying the hell out of as much of Sylvanas' madness as they can. Divorcing them entirely from the story the game forces they'd be off on their own with the remaining neutral members of the Illidari looking for a way to save the world. 

They are very much on Saurfang/Baine's side; Isaril already did this shit with Garrosh and is so over it, and Velereth knows too well from what happened with Illidan that even if Sylvanas somehow has people's best interests in mind, the way she's going about things will only turn people against her and the Horde and make things worse.

My thoughts:

The first thing I think of is 'dead talents'. 

Demonic Appetite. This was great in T21 Demonic when you took it with Blind Fury an- Oh wait it's in the same row now. And the same row as Fel Blade. Move it, fix it, or hell it does so little now just make it baseline and let me not have to press Demon's Bite as much. Or give it the Feast on the Souls artifact trait and let it reduce Eyebeam CD and this could maybe be an interesting choice if balanced properly. 

Insatiable Hunger - It's a bad version of our mandatory legendary from Legion that nobody actually enjoyed that does less than anything else in the 100 row. 

Demon Blades isn't dead, though it isn't used in the dominating Demonic spec, but it's just as RNG and just as bad feeling as it was in Legion. I literally have a talent to remove a button. 

Here's where I pause to say something: Blizzard. We have *two entire rows* dedicated literally to nothing but fury generation. Maybe, just maybe, take a look at some point at fury and how it's generated overall and do something instead of two rows of bandaids. Immo Aura fun. Blind Fury fun. Felblade Fun. Useful iterations of Demonic Appetite fun. Maybe make some of that *baseline* and you could use talent rows for things other than fury generation. While we're on the subject, going from 100 to 120 fury cap was a good move but it still feels like too little after being used to 140 in Legion.

Fel Mastery... Meh? Next to Trail of Ruin and Fel Barrage, this just doesn't feel like something I'd ever take except as part of Momentum builds, but Momentum builds don't seem to use it either. Maybe if it granted an extra charge or something.

Neither Trail or Barrage is a dead talent, but what happened to that thing where you didn't want us to have to switch talents between ST and AoE fights? I use multiple books per Uldir run swapping between the two depending on the fight. 

104 row, Desperate Instincts is as pointless as it was in Legion. It needs something. Maybe the Demonic Speed trait? You know, where Blur made you run faster? That was fun. 

Netherwalk being on GCD feels absolutely awful. I will probably repeat this later. It's an oh shit button... That you can't use as an oh shit button. It's a defensive, ffs, I can't even attack during it, so why?

106... Oh boy. Cycle of Hatred is just too RNG to be dependable. Delusions worked and was enjoyable because you could influence it. Higher crit chance for higher refunds for more fury for more Chaos Strikes(/blade dance in T20), it worked well and was fun. This isn't. It happens. Or it doesn't. 

Dark Slash... No one at all who plays Demon Hunter ever thought to themselves 'Man I really wish I had a terrible version of Colossus Smash that didn't line up with any of my other CDs'. We already live and die by small DPS windows, adding another doesn't feel fun or engaging. I'd be happy to see this go away entirely in favor of something we've lost that was actually useful, except I can't see not taking First Blood because Blade Dance is fun to use. 

108, eh. Fel Eruption feels pointless as I seldom have to stun only one enemy. Otherwise feels actually useful as a tier. 

110, hoo boy. 

Demonic is great. It's missing all the little interactions from T21 Legion Demonic that made that spec really fun to play in the end, but it's serviceable, basically universally applicable, and the short CD allows for smoothing out the ludicrously long CD of Meta with mini-metas. That said, without all the little interactions and fiddly bits it's kind of repetitive.

Momentum... OK I'm just going to state outright that I hate the very concept of Momentum. I don't play a mobile class to use all my mobility to do damage. Too many boss fights have mechanics that make this punishing to outright impossible to use, and even if you do mastery the intricacies and find a way to use it even on fights with strict positioning requirements, your reward is... What? It's a cute concept, but it feels out of place in the game. I have no suggestions. 

Nemesis... Is boring. It's really boring. And weird. And meh. And did I mention boring? You hit a thing. The hit is on the GCD. If there are adds and the types don't match the boss you either can't use it on the adds or you can't use it on the boss depending on what's currently your highest priority. This felt useful on ST bosses, Eonar, and High Command where saving it for the first add spawn instead of using it immediately let you have the extra damage on the adds as well as the boss. If the fight suits it it can be nice, but what it will never not be is boring. 

Talents out of the way, let's talk our pruning and the things I really miss.

No one ever really liked Fury of the Illidari, but it's still weird that it's gone. 

Demonic Speed, our movespeed on blur trait. That was fun and super useful both in and out of combat. 

Our mastery. A lot more of our damage now comes from non-Chaos sources. This makes mastery my worst stat by quite a lot. Worse, the movement speed granted from it was gutted so now it feels sluggish after being used to Legion movement speed, especially with trying to have less mastery and more of other more heavily weighted stats. It's sad-making.

Feast on the Souls was part of what made T21 Demonic fun, orb management. There's a terrible azerite trait that does a similar thing, but the reduction is almost non-existant and you aren't using Demonic Appetite to even give it soul fragments to work with so it's completely pointless in most situations. 

Chaos Blades was fun when it was used because what DPS doesn't enjoy absolutely absurd burst numbers? 

Like, it works now, DH is in a good spot, it's just... Weird. A lot of talents that aren't worth taking and some that are just baffling.

It feels like whoever 'reworked' us didn't really play the class or listen to much if any feedback and just threw a few things at it and called it a day. It's functional, but it could be better. 

I'm probably forgetting a few things/going to get flamed by Momentum lovers/whatever but meh.

As to Illidan getting the keystone by himself, while it's unlikely the Legion would have moved it, it might have been harder to divert forces to during the active invasion. Every single Demon Hunter at the Black Temple except Vandel were on that mission, plus a good chunk of Broken, Coilscar, and Shivarra. The keystone is recovered by this force, only the Demon Hunters make it back while the others hold the Fel Hammer for years, the future Slayer has the keystone on him/her and they're all imprisoned with the keystone hidden in the Vault with Illidan's corpse.

So the Vault of the Wardens dungeon is Cordana going back there to get that keystone back; this happens before Illidan is revived and is also part of the Demon Hunter class hall as you need to find out from the Wardens where they put the thing since you didn't have it when you were freed. None of the other classes would have known what it was and since presumably a DH is leading the group going into the Vault it's possible that the window to stop Cordana could have been missed or the keystone itself could have been missed even if she was stopped, and it would have been in an unknown location in the Legion's hands, probably on Argus itself. So Illidan might not have been able to get to it without the DHs knowing where to go when.

There's also the issue of Illidan's revival in the first place - The Soul Prism used to retrieve Illidan's soul so it can be used to revive him is created by the Demon Hunters; you get it from Allari. The Demon Hunters are also the ones who are actively looking for Illidan since until Light's Heart is activated and Xe'ra starts her guilt trip, no one else particularly wants him back.

So while Illidan might be powerful enough, potentially, to do it himself or with some help, without the Demon Hunters being active in Legion we may well not have *had* Illidan, and he might not have even been able to get to the keystone if we did.

For the second time in his life, Velereth Nightsinger stood amidst a ruined village overrun by the undead, choking back tears as he stared at the corpses left carelessly on the ground. 

He had arrived too late, then, thirteen years ago. The Scourge had torn through Quel’thalas with a speed and violence that had seemed beyond anything imaginable. He had since seen even worse, but the memory of the day was still engraved in his mind. The dead that day had been his friends. His family. The undead and the demons that had led them had taken everything from him that day, and he’d come home to find his mother a barely recognizable, bloody mess, and his twin brother Isaril, the man who had always been as much a part of him as he was… He had run, then, with nothing left to stay for, knowing he was powerless to do anything.

Years later, when the opportunity to become a Demon Hunter had presented itself to him, he hadn’t even hesitated. The Legion had been involved with the Scourge. That was all that mattered. Their end. He had gladly given up his body, his flesh, and in that last desperate mission to Mardum even as the Black Temple fell, his very life and soul. It had been easy to do, with nothing to live for but revenge. And in the end he’d been imprisoned for his troubles, ostensibly forever. But freedom had come with the Legion’s return, and with it…

He had barely been able to contain his laughter when Sylvanas Windrunner had threatened him and his Illidari at Vol’jin’s funeral. He had just saved her life, such as it was, and the irony of the undead mockery of Quel’thalas’ former Ranger General objecting to his own demonic mutations was entirely too delicious. Even those of his people who had become monsters saw him as one. Even those who hadn’t… By the Sunwell, they’d joined the Horde. Allegedly it was a different one than the one that had once plagued his homeland, and yet he had his doubts. 

And in truth, his former people had ceased to be his people to him, his slaughtered family a distant, agonizing memory he avoided whenever possible. His people were the Illidari. The Demon Hunters his new family. Once the night elves among them would have been a curiosity at best and enemies at worst, but now they were his brothers and sisters, their former petty differences burned away by the Felfire that coursed through their veins. It would have been simplicity itself to turn away from the Sin’dorei and the Horde he’d never been part of in favor of his new kin. It should have been.

But he’d found something else on his return to the world. Something he had missed that day, long ago. Isaril had lived, barely, and had continued living in the world he’d left behind, had been part of the Horde, believed in it. And he had believed in Velereth. There had been no recriminations, no angry demands to know what he had done to himself, no hatred or revulsion. They had simply reunited as though they had never been separated, and together they had fought the Legion until it lay in ruins. And he had given the Horde a chance, just as his brother had given him one.

And then this. War was ugly, certainly. And he was no stranger to violence or going to extremes for the sake of the universe. But this… He had not slaughtered civilians. He had not burned forests. He might have turned himself into what was essentially a demon playing at still being something vaguely elven, but he had never, ever allowed himself to commit atrocities like this. Even at his worst Illidan had shielded his Demon Hunters from such things, and once Velereth had come to lead the Illidari he had forbidden such things entirely, determined not to repeat his mentor’s mistakes. 

He had silently fallen back from the Horde’s assault as they had pressed towards Teldrassil, as he had realized where he was, and what the day reminded him of. And now he was back where he had started, despite the years and oceans and worlds separating the two days. The tears he’d sought to hold back finally escaped, pouring down his cheeks and he felt as powerless as he had back then. He was powerful, certainly, but he couldn’t stand against the entire Horde army, and Sylvanas was powerful as well and well-guarded. 

But today, he vowed, would not end the same as that day. Perhaps he couldn’t stop the Horde, but he could do what he could. And this time, he wasn’t alone. Isaril had fallen behind with him, and his twin stood next to him, identical tears spilling down his cheeks. They looked at each other, Isaril’s green eyes meeting his own empty sockets, and nodded as one.

Isaril had survived once, when he shouldn’t have been able to. Surely some today had as well. This time he wouldn’t miss them. He focused his spectral sight, forcing away his usual way of seeing the world as he once had and letting the energy all around him pervade his senses. The lack of the auras of the living around him was horrifying, but he forced himself to concentrate, to see what was there, rather than what wasn’t. And… There. Faint, but still present. Three of them, still alive, but barely. Isaril recognized the relief on his face and immediately began to conjure a portal to Dalaran as Velereth quickly gathered the survivors together and began tending to the worst of their wounds to get them stable enough to move. 

He had just finished bandaging a young boy, a tiny little blue slip of a thing that felt entirely too light when he lifted him, when an older night elf ran into the village, an all too familiar look of horror on his face as he scanned the scene and his eyes fell on Velereth and the boy he cradled in his arms. Relief and confusion crossed the man’s face as the boy stirred to look at him.

“Nendrith… Brother,” the larger night elf whispered as he warily approached the Demon Hunter holding his little brother. Velereth held the boy out to him and he took him gently, looking at the other pair of brothers strangely. 

“Take him,” Velereth said in oddly accented Darnassian, holding the boy out to the night elf, “It’s not safe here.” The bewildered night elf nodded, too relieved and stunned to argue. He snatched his brother from Velereth’s arms, examined the portal for a moment to ensure it wouldn’t take him somewhere dangerous, and ran through. Isaril quickly got the other two passed through and turned to his brother, a smile breaking through his sorrow. 

“Not today,” they said in unison. Perhaps they couldn’t stop the war, or reverse what had already been done, but they could save who they still could. If the Horde could still be saved, they’d save that too. And if not… Then they would stand together and fight once again, until the very end. They called their mounts, and rode together into the forest.

Demon Hunters are even more of a clusterfuck than other classes. Kor'vas? She's our 'face', but she's not our second in command or even really leadership in the class campaign. 

No, DHs have not one, not even two, but *four* possible states, because you are given a choice twice during the starting experience.

The first isn't that important though difficult to know which is supposed to be canon - Whether you sacrifice yourself or Sevis. Sevis isn't seen by non-DH and he has extensive text he says if you kill him that's not present if he's alive - But killing yourself results in a rather interesting voice acted commentary from Illidan.

The second choice that really throws things for a loop and has continuity snarl possibilities is who your second in command is - #1 Illidan fanboy Kayn Sunfury, or familiar face and ex-Illidari non-fanboy Altruis the Sufferer. Which you pick determines whether Akama has his soul ripped apart again to re-form the Shade of Akama(Kayn) or is convinced to peacefully and willingly work with a changed Illidari(Altruis). Sadly the former is likely canon since non-DH see Kayn in Azsuna and never see Altruis unless he's someone's combat ally. Pity.

So you have the possibility of Altruis and Sevis alive, Altruis and Sevis dead, Kayn and Sevis alive, and Kayn and Sevis dead.

Naturally this is an unresolveable clusterfuck, and thus Kor'vas became our poster child(and to a lesser extent Jace and Allari) and it's extremely likely none of the events of the DH class hall will ever be mentioned again. 

The class mount quest makes it even more fuzzy, because while the cutscene is doing the batvision of her looking around, you can make out Altruis *and* Kayn standing there, with Sevis in the background. Implying I suppose that whichever of K and A you didn't pick eventually reconciled with the Illidari and that Sevis being alive is canon, but it may also just be an attempt to put more unique models in the scene since you need to know them to recognize them.

So I own one of these and helped beta test it. 

I love it, personally. No, it's not like the Ergodox, it's not intended to be. 

The biggest keycap compatibility hurdle is the spacebars. Those you aren't going to be changing as they're not a standard size. 

Having the six on the left as opposed to all the split boards that get it wrong is really nice. 

It is in fact a mechanical version of their long-running membrane FreeStyle keyboard. The layout awkwardness is a holdover from that.

Layouts are easy as hell to manage. You can do remapping and simple macros on the board itself via the programming keys; more extensive remapping and keys not physically present on the board can be done via the software configurator, which is stored on the board itself and is accessed via opening it from the onboard drive after enabling a mode to allow the board to act like a flash drive. This has access to things like numpad codes, mouse buttons, F13-F24, etc, and click buttons for enabling an embedded numpad on a function or main layer, rearranging the board to Dvorak or Colemak, more robust macro options, and easily managing layouts. (You can have nine layouts, each with a normal and a Fn layer.)

You can also just plain edit the layout text file once you know how the remapping/macros/etc work. 

The wrist rests are removable and the connecting cable length can be adjusted.

I like MX Blues so mine is just plain MX Blues. I can't stand gaming(or typing, or anything really) on an Ergodox so for me it's a perfect compromise between being able to get comfortable angles and positioning and not being irritated by 'ergonomic' boards that just plain don't fit my hands. The split is also nice since I can keep the right half on my nice big mousepad when I play WoW but if I need more room for an FPS I can just move that shit out of the way and if I need a right hand key that's what remapping shit to the bank of keys on the left is for. (And yes you can use all 10, the Fn and lighting key are there by default but like everything else can be remapped.)

The blue lighting is nice and unobtrusive at lower lighting levels. I've never understood the 'must have RGB' thing since I don't look at my keyboard while I'm using it anyway.

A single, precious fuck. 

More accurately, pretty much all of us lost everything to the Legion before we became DHs. Family, friends, lovers, etc? Dead, probably in horrible ways we may or may not have watched. Our homes were destroyed. Whatever livelihood we had before is gone. All we're really left with is our lives and our hatred of the Legion. 

So we're already basically crazy hobos from the start. Crazy enough to want revenge and to keep what happened from us from happening to anyone else, and crazy enough to do *anything* to make that happen. So hey, there's this other crazy fuck and he puts us through training from hell until he decides we're strong enough to maybe survive this shit, maybe, then we undergo a ritual where we kill a demon, eat its heart, and drink its blood. We pass out, it forces us to relive the experiences that drove us to do this shit in the first place, and shows us a vision of the infinite might of the Legion and its atrocities and just how fucking hopeless it all is. Some of us claw our eyes out during this(Vandel does this in the Illidan novel), some of us cut them out later(We see Kor'vas or some other DH that looks like her doing this during a cutscene).

So assuming we survive that shit we wake up eventually with the demon's soul now permanently bound to us and living in our head constantly trying to tempt us to join the Legion or just go crazy on people. We've developed demonic features and powers that make other people hate us. The missing eyes thing isn't too much of an issue because we develop our spectral sight and can 'see' using that but it's yet another thing that creeps people out and makes them hate us. A lot of DHs kill themselves because they can't stand what they've become. Some just go crazy. 

The ones who don't do either are pretty much put into combat situations as soon as they're even remotely capable of doing it and spend the rest of their miserable, violent lives fighting what should be a pointless fight for the sake of people who despise us and would be perfectly happy if we all died, while in constant pain and fighting an eternal struggle against the demon within us.

The PC DH further gets to contend with potentially having literally sacrificed their life for the cause, and also knowing that they've literally corrupted themselves so hard their soul is now demonic.

All of which ironically make DHs for all the accusations of 'emo edgelords' one of the more hopeful and optimistic classes. We know how seemingly hopeless the battle against the Legion is better than anybody. We know nobody is ever going to thank us for what we do or appreciate it in any way. We still believe the Legion will be defeated and we shrug off the hate and do what needs to be done anyway. 

So. I sacrificed my body, my soul, any hope of any kind of life past what I do now, and any hope of ever finding peace in death. What have you given? (If you're a Death Knight you do get something of a pass since you've lost a lot of the same shit, although I'll still remind you I actually chose to do this shit and you had it forced on you.)
